_comment: Execution-environment factors for the combinatorial test matrix, plus the policy that decides how much of the matrix each risk band earns. Factors marked source='real' are parsed out of BehaviorContextMatrix.kt in the tree; those marked 'stubbed' are plausible placeholders for the PoC.
_stub_note: Real minSdk/targetSdk are computed in mach's Python build config rather than declared in the gradle files, and the device pool would come from Firebase Test Lab / the Autophone config. Both are stubbed here.

infrastructure_factors.name: ApiLevel
infrastructure_factors.origin: Placeholder. Real values live in mach build config; the shipping matrix should come from the Play Console API-level distribution.
infrastructure_factors.rationale: Android behaviour changes at API boundaries (scoped storage at 29, notification permission at 33, foreground service types at 34) break features asymmetrically.

infrastructure_factors.name: DeviceClass
infrastructure_factors.origin: Phone and Tablet are real levels in BehaviorContextMatrix.kt; Foldable is a stub.
infrastructure_factors.rationale: Layout and navigation diverge by form factor; tablets use a different toolbar and tabs-tray presentation.

infrastructure_factors.name: BuildVariant
infrastructure_factors.origin: Placeholder for the real product flavors.
infrastructure_factors.rationale: Secret settings, debug menus and some Nimbus defaults differ by variant, so a Nightly-only pass can miss a Release-only path.

infrastructure_factors.name: Network
infrastructure_factors.rationale: Offline paths are a common source of unhandled states in downloads, sync and search.

infrastructure_factors.name: Theme
infrastructure_factors.rationale: Cheap to vary and catches contrast and drawable-tint regressions.

_allocation_comment: How much matrix a feature earns is a function of its FMEA band. Spending 3-way coverage on an acceptable-band feature is how a test matrix becomes unaffordable; spending only the default config on an action-required feature is how a release ships broken.

action-required.rationale: High severity and high churn. 3-way catches interaction faults that pairwise provably cannot, and the empirical fault-detection literature puts 3-way in the 90%+ range.

review.rationale: Pairwise. Most reported combinatorial faults are 2-way, so this is the standard value-for-money point.

acceptable.rationale: Baseline configuration only. Enough to notice a total break, not enough to characterise it. Strength 0 means one representative config rather than a combinatorial array.

_cost_comment: Device-minutes multipliers, stubbed. Real numbers would come from Firebase Test Lab billing or Treeherder task durations.
